inspectionOrder: Original RAW200 PNG was the first and only image opened before inventory and authoring; no existing modern fig200 spec, SVG or raster was inspected.

sourceFacts.observation: One shallow plano-convex lens cross-section. A straight horizontal upper face joins the two ends of one smooth downward-convex lower surface. Scattered diagonal marks indicate glass inside the lens; these are material hatching, not a measured grid.

A long horizontal plate lies below the lens, with oblique material hatching beneath its upper surface. The lowest central point of the curved lens meets the plate. Air gaps open to the left and right of that contact.

An unlabeled upper vertex on the central vertical line joins an off-center point on the left lower lens surface by an oblique straight segment. That segment is labeled R. A second straight vertical segment runs from the same upper vertex to the center contact and is also labeled R.

The left surface point joins the central vertical line by a horizontal straight segment labeled r_k. Its intersection with the central vertical is above the center contact and below the upper curvature-center vertex. These three vertices form a right triangle: the oblique R is the hypotenuse and the vertical leg is only the upper part of the full vertical R. The pixels do not contain an explicit square right-angle marker.

At the left surface point a short vertical line descends to the plate. The adjacent h_k label denotes the local vertical lens-to-plate gap. The horizontal r_k segment is at this surface point's height, so its central endpoint is h_k above center contact.

Four mathematical label occurrences only: R on the oblique radius, R on the full vertical radius, r_k on the horizontal ring-radius segment, and h_k beside the local gap. No point letters, numerical measurements, units, formula, light ray, ring count, spectral color, caption or other subfigure appears inside this PNG.

modernAdditionsPlanned: Regularize the hand-drawn lower surface to an exact circular arc, consistent with the approved curvature-radius text; construction coordinates are illustrative, not given numeric data.
Use a restrained material tint for lens glass and regular plate hatching, not old-book texture or a fictional measured grid.
Add a small explicit right-angle marker, English Lens / Glass plate labels, and clear thickness dimension guides if needed for legibility.
Render the k subscripts as separate deterministic text nodes so even the subscript text has a checked final font size of at least 16 px.
